## Summary

**BANK** (Bank): Prefix for legacy instructions.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | Inform the next instruction apollo-registers are used. |
| Syntax | `- none -` |
| Short | Prefix for legacy instructions. |
| Description | Bank gives older instructions more bits to select more registers. |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–12 | `0111` |
| 1 | 11–9 | c |
| 1 | 8 | `1` |
| 1 | 7–6 | S |
| 1 | 5–4 | C |
| 1 | 3–2 | A |
| 1 | 1–0 | B |

- AA extends 1st bankable source operand from 3bit to 5bit. (From 8 to 32 options)
- BB extends 1st bankable destination operand.
- CCccc is xored to BBbbb to create a third operand.

```text
If CCccc <> 0  then  BBbbb xor CCccc → DDddd
    instr a ? b → d
else
    instr a ? b → b
endif
```

- AA & BB & DD:

| Value | Data & Float | ea mode (Address & Index) \* |
|---|---|---|
| `00` | original | original |
| `01` | E0 - E7 | B0-7 |
| `10` | E8 - E15 | Xn → E0-7 or B0-7 |
| `11` | E16- E23 | B0-7 & Xn → E0-7 or B0-7 |

- SS Size is the length of the whole bundle = opcode length + bank\_length *(grayed out in the original)*
- 0 = 4 bytes, 1 = 6 bytes, 2 = 8 bytes, 3 = 10 bytes *(grayed out in the original)*

### Notes

- \* Addressed ea mode is not implemented yet.
- Size SS is not needed anymore. Will be used to expand instruction options.
- For a single register operand instruction (and the Dbcc counter) the register is selected by BB. AA is ignored. Set AA = BB

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no BANK. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- DON'T use banked address modes (AA/BB = 10 or 11 for the ea): the manual marks them not implemented yet.
